problem.description: One sentence, two at most, on what is wrong or missing today.

solution.description: One sentence, two at most, on the outcome the ticket asks for, not a design.

item.description: The thing to deliver, in a few plain words.

quote.description: The ticket's own words for it, verbatim and short.

section.description: Where the quote comes from: the Solution, the Acceptance Criteria, or elsewhere in the description when the ticket has no such sections.

items.description: Every distinct thing the ticket asks to deliver, from the Solution and Acceptance Criteria. The Problem is context, not an item.
One line: the ticket key or outside fact, its status when known, and what it blocks.

question.description: One short line asking what to build, ending in a question mark.

items.description: A few words; does not repeat the question.

options.description: Two to four choices the developer picks from; empty only when no choice fits.

recommended.description: The recommended option, copied exactly from options; the suggested answer when options is empty.

why.description: The reason for the recommendation, in a few words.

items.description: What this option leads to, in under 15 words, written evenly with the others.

consequences.description: One line per option, in the same order as options; empty when options is empty.

key.description: The other ticket's key, from the list of other open tickets.

why.description: One sentence naming the criterion, behaviour or file that ties the tickets.

relations.description: How this ticket depends on, repeats, contradicts or collides with the other open tickets. Empty when none do.
